The main purpose of the research is to broaden the effective absorbing bandwidth of radar absorbing coatings.
Carbon fiber is used as the filler and polyurethane as the matrix in the CFPURAC.
Multi-layer CFPURAC is prepared by matching carbon fiber/polyurethane radar absorbing coating with polyurethane coating as a wave-transmitting material.
Scanning electron microscope (SEM) and metallography microscope are used to characterize the microstructure of the filler and coating.
The radar wave reflectivity is tested using a vector network analyzer (VNA).
The absorbing property is influenced by the length and content of carbon fiber in the coating, as well as the matching order and thickness of various absorbing layers.
The optimal configuration achieves an effective absorbing bandwidth of up to 13.1 GHz, covering the frequency range of 4.9 GHz to 18 GHz.

Increasing the carbon fiber content generally improves the absorbing property up to a certain point, but excessive content can lead to a continuous conductive network, reducing the effectiveness of microwave absorption.

Shorter carbon fibers may not provide effective microwave absorption, while longer fibers can enhance the ability to form a conductive network, but if too long, they can form a continuous network that hinders absorption.
The polyurethane coating acts as a wave-transmitting material, helping to match the impedance and improve the overall absorbing property of the multi-layer structure.
The matching thickness affects the impedance matching and the effective absorbing bandwidth, with optimal thickness leading to the best absorbing performance.
The maximum reflection loss achieved is -41 dB, with an effective absorbing bandwidth of 8.6–18 GHz when the matching thickness is 2.5 mm.
The sequence of absorbing layers, particularly placing the high-frequency absorbing layer on top and the low-frequency absorbing layer below, results in better overall absorbing performance.
Increasing the matching thickness generally extends the effective absorbing bandwidth to lower frequencies, but excessive thickness can reduce performance in higher frequency bands.
The wave-transmitting material helps to match the impedance between layers, reducing reflection and enhancing the overall absorbing property of the coating.
